points.title: Column addition method
points.must: Line up on the right, add from the right with carries written above the next column; a worked example (01101101 + 00110110 = 10100011) checked in denary.

points.title: Checking in denary
points.must: Convert both numbers and the answer to denary to check (109 + 54 = 163).

points.title: Definition of overflow
points.must: The result is too large for the number of bits available, e.g. more than 255 in an 8-bit register.

points.title: What happens in overflow
points.must: The carry out of the leftmost column (9th bit) is lost; the register keeps the true result minus 256; the overflow flag is set.

points.title: Overflow example
points.must: A worked example such as 200 + 100 → stored 00101100 = 44, or 240 + 31 → 15.

points.title: Avoiding overflow
points.must: Use more bits (e.g. a 16-bit register) or check values before adding.

points.title: Rules of binary multiplication
points.must: 0×0 = 0, 0×1 = 0, 1×1 = 1 — each row is a copy of the number or zeros.

points.title: Shift-and-add method
points.must: For each multiplier bit from the right, copy or write zeros, shift one more place left each row, then add the partial products.

points.title: Multiplication example
points.must: A worked example such as 1101 × 101 = 1000001 (13 × 5 = 65) with partial products, checked in denary.

points.title: Logical shift
points.must: Bits move left or right; empty places filled with 0; left n places = × 2ⁿ, right n places = ÷ 2ⁿ (remainder lost).

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Forgetting carries; not shifting partial products; starting from the left bit of the multiplier; keeping the 9th bit in an 8-bit answer.
